rationale: The workflow already implements the applicable evidence-supported optimizations. Concurrency with cancel-in-progress: true (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) already cancels superseded runs for the same workflow/branch. Dependency downloads are already cached via setup-ruby-flash bundler-cache: true (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE), keyed to the lockfile/environment, so adding a second actions/cache for vendor/bundle is contraindicated by the pattern's "An equivalent cache already exists" condition and by the P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE experiment's equivalent-cache setup. fail-fast is GitHub Actions' default (true), so remaining matrix jobs are already cancelled on failure (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) without any workflow change. The 30-minute job timeout is not a source of waste because all observed CI runs complete in roughly 1-2 minutes, far below the limit; lowering it would save no VM time for fast jobs and risks false timeouts on cold or slow valid runs (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT contraindication: valid slow runs may exceed the proposed limit, and representative history is too limited to set a safe bound). No safe, supported change remains that preserves build/test coverage.
